Travellers should not return to their families at night before wives can groom; the Prophet asked newly married Jabir why not a virgin, urging him to seek children.
At Uhud, Fatima washed the blood from the Prophet's face while Ali brought water in his shield, and ash of a burnt palm-leaf mat was put into the wound.
Ibn Abbas, young but close to the Prophet, saw him lead the Eid prayer and sermon, then urge the women to give alms, and they threw their jewellery to Bilal.
Aisha recalls Abu Bakr scolding her and poking her flank while she kept still, as the Prophet's head lay on her thigh.
The Prophet had Ibn Umar, who divorced his wife during menses, take her back until a later purity, then keep or divorce her; that divorce was counted as one.
When Al-Jaun's daughter, brought to the Prophet as a bride, sought refuge with Allah from him, he told her to return to her family, giving her two linen dresses.
A menses divorce counted; Uwaimir divorced thrice after li'an; a thrice-divorced wife returns only after another husband consummates marriage; the option the Prophet gave his wives was no divorce.
Making one's wife unlawful is not divorce; the Prophet's wives played a trick, claiming a bad smell, until he gave up honey, and verses of Surah 66 came down.
Allah forgives the Prophet's followers evil thoughts not acted upon or spoken, and Qatada said a divorce made only in the mind has no effect.
A married man of Bani Aslam confessed illegal sexual intercourse four times; the Prophet asked if he was insane, then had him stoned, caught at Al-Harra when he fled.
Thabit bin Qais's wife, finding no fault in his character or religion yet unable to stay with him, returned his garden, and the Prophet had him divorce her.
The Prophet said Banu Al-Mughira had asked his leave to let Ali marry their daughter, and he gave no leave.
Freed and given the choice, Barira left her slave husband Mughith despite his tears and the Prophet's intercession; wala goes to whoever frees, and alms given her became a gift.
Ibn Umar held marrying a woman who calls Jesus her Lord unlawful; an emigrant woman from warring pagans could marry after one menses; Umar and Iyad divorced wives who remarried.
The Prophet tested believing women who came as emigrants, as Allah ordered, and accepted their pledge of allegiance by word alone, his hand never touching a woman's.
The Prophet ended his oath of abstention from his wives after twenty-nine days; Ibn Umar said after Ila's four months a husband must keep his wife well or divorce her.
Asked about lost property, the Prophet said a stray sheep may be taken, a stray camel left alone, and found money announced for a year before it is kept.
Riding in Tawaf, the Prophet pointed at the Black Stone corner saying Allahu Akbar, and showed with his fingers the opening made in the wall of Gog and Magog.
On Friday there is a moment when a Muslim who is praying and asks Allah for some good is granted it.
Dying, a girl whose head a Jew had crushed for her silver ornaments nodded at his name, and the Prophet had his head crushed between two stones.
Pointing towards the East, the Prophet said afflictions would emerge from there.
Pointing east, the Prophet said a fasting person breaks the fast when night falls from there, and that Bilal's adhan does not mark dawn or stop the pre-dawn meal.
The generous and the miser are like two men in iron cloaks: the generous one's spreads to cover him when he spends, while the miser's rings stick tight.
The Prophet ranked the best Ansar families, Banu An-Najjar first, then Banu Abdil Ash-hal, Banu Al-Harith and Banu Sa'ida, adding there is good in every Ansar family.
Holding up two fingers, the Prophet said his advent and the Hour are as close as these.
With his fingers the Prophet showed that a month is sometimes thirty days and sometimes twenty-nine.
Pointing to Yemen the Prophet said faith is there; towards the East, among Rabi'a and Mudar, are harsh camel-herders heedless of religion, where the two sides of Satan's head appear.
Showing his middle and index fingers, the Prophet said he and the one who looks after an orphan will be like this in Paradise.
When a man said a black child had been born to him, the Prophet, likening it to a grey camel among red ones, said the colour may come from heredity.
Husbands accusing wives of adultery swore li'an with them before the Prophet, who urged repentance and separated them; the mahr was not returned and the child was the mother's.
Rifa'a's divorced wife, remarried to an impotent man, was told she could not return to Rifa'a until the second husband consummated the marriage.
Subai'a al-Aslamiya, widowed while pregnant, was told by the Prophet after giving birth that she could marry, and she did.
Aisha faulted a divorced woman for leaving her husband's house, and rebuked Fatima bint Qais for saying such women get no housing or upkeep, since Fatima left an unsafe place.
Leaving Mecca after Hajj, the Prophet found Safiyya sad at her tent; learning she had done Tawaf al-Ifada on the day of sacrifice, he said she could depart.
Ma'qil, refusing to let his divorced sister remarry her former husband, yielded when verse 2:232 came down; Ibn Umar, who divorced in menses, was ordered to take his wife back.
A woman mourns her husband four months and ten days and anyone else three days at most, without kohl, perfume or dyed clothes; verse 2:240 on widows' residence is explained.
The Prophet forbade the price of a dog, a soothsayer's fee and earnings from prostitution, including a slave girl's, and cursed tattooing, taking or giving riba, and picture-makers.
Ibn Umar reported that the Prophet separated a couple after li'an, saying one of them lies, and told the husband his mahr could not be taken back.
Spending on one's family for Allah's reward is charity, even a morsel for a wife; caring for widows equals jihad; start with dependants; the Prophet stored his family's yearly food.
Umar reminded Ali and Abbas, claiming the Prophet's estate, that what prophets leave is charity, not inheritance, and held them to manage it as the Prophet and Abu Bakr had.
